title: How Much Does Attic Cleaning Cost? Key Factors
h1: How Much Does Attic Cleaning Cost? Factors to Check Before a Quote
description: Attic cleaning cost depends on attic size, access, how much insulation comes out, rodent damage and what goes back in. Here is what to check before a quote.
quick_answer: Attic cleaning cost depends on the size of the attic, how easy it is to reach and work in, how much insulation has to be removed, the level of rodent or water contamination, whether entry points need sealing and what new insulation goes back in. An on-site inspection is the only way to get an accurate number.
body:
Attic cleaning prices vary a lot from one home to the next, and a phone quote without an inspection is usually a guess. Two homes with the same square footage can need very different amounts of work. Knowing what drives the cost helps you understand an estimate and compare apples to apples.

What affects the cost the most?

Attic size and layout

Larger attics take more time and material. Layout matters too. A wide-open attic with good headroom is faster to work in than a low-pitched roof with tight corners, multiple sections or vaulted areas that are hard to reach.

Access

Most Southern California attics are reached through a small hatch in a hallway closet or the garage. If the hatch is small, blocked by shelving or located far from where the work happens, the crew spends more time moving hoses and material. A furnace or ductwork in the attic can also limit where crews can walk and work.

How much insulation comes out

Full removal of old insulation takes more labor than spot removal in a few contaminated areas. The type and depth of insulation matter too. Deep blown-in insulation takes longer to vacuum out than a single layer of batts.

Level of contamination

A dusty attic with old insulation is a different job from one with years of rodent droppings, urine and nesting material. Heavy contamination calls for more careful removal, more cleaning and more sanitizing. Water damage or mold can add more work as well.

Rodent proofing and repairs

If rodents got in, the openings they used need to be found and sealed. The number of entry points, their location and whether vents or screens need replacing all affect the price. Chewed wiring or damaged ducts may need separate repairs.

New insulation

Most attic cleanings end with fresh insulation. The type, the depth and whether air sealing is done first all change the cost.

What should a good estimate include?

When you compare quotes, look for a clear breakdown of:

  • Removal of old insulation, including whether it's full or partial.
  • Removal of droppings, nesting material and debris.
  • Sanitizing or deodorizing treatment.
  • Rodent entry point sealing, with the areas identified.
  • Air sealing before new insulation goes in.
  • Type and depth of new insulation.
  • Protection of your home during the work and cleanup afterward.
  • Disposal of removed material.

A low price that leaves out sealing entry points or skips sanitizing can end up costing more if rodents come back or odors linger.

What can you check before getting a quote?

A few quick observations help us give you a more accurate estimate:

  1. Where is the attic access? Note whether it's in a closet, hallway or garage and roughly how large it is.
  2. Have you heard scratching or seen droppings? Note where and when.
  3. Any odors? Musty or ammonia-like smells in certain rooms or closets.
  4. Roof or plumbing leaks? Past or present leaks that may have soaked insulation.
  5. Is the HVAC equipment or ductwork in the attic? This affects access and whether duct inspection makes sense.
  6. Do you know your attic square footage? It's often close to the footprint of the top floor.

Please don't climb into the attic yourself if you suspect rodents. Droppings and nesting material can carry diseases, and attics are easy to fall through between the joists.

Can you save money on attic cleaning?

A few things can help:

  • Don't wait. A small rodent problem caught early costs less than years of buildup.
  • Combine work. Doing cleaning, rodent proofing, air sealing and new insulation in one visit saves on repeat setup and labor.
  • Look for rebates. Utility programs for insulation and air sealing come and go, so ask what's available.
  • Check current offers. We post discounts on our specials page.

How do you get an accurate price?

We'll inspect the attic, take photos so you can see what we see, and explain the scope before giving you a written estimate. Learn more about our attic cleaning and insulation service. Estimates are free.
faqs: Why do attic cleaning quotes vary so much?
Quotes differ based on attic size, access, contamination level, whether entry points are sealed and what insulation goes back in. Compare the scope line by line, not just the total.
Is attic cleaning worth the cost?

If the attic has rodent contamination, water damage or badly compressed insulation, cleaning and reinsulating can remove odors, cut down on pests and help the home hold its temperature. A clean attic with good insulation may not need anything.
Does attic cleaning include new insulation?
It often does, but not always. Make sure your estimate says whether new insulation is included, along with the type and depth.
Can I get an estimate without an inspection?
A rough range might be possible, but an accurate estimate needs someone to see the attic, the access and the level of contamination. Our estimates are free.
